section: A.P. Reorganisation Act 2014 - structure, schedules and key provisions
subsections: Act structure - parts, sections, schedules and the subject of each Part
Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 was enacted primarily under which Article of the Constitution of India?
accepted.x: The Act was enacted under Article 3, which empowers Parliament to form a new State out of an existing State. Article 2 deals with admission or establishment of new States.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely related constitutional provisions rather than relying on the subject of the legislation alone.
accepted.sec: Act structure - parts, sections, schedules and the subject of each Part  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Part I of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Preliminary provisions, including definitions and the population ratio based on Census 2011
Apportionment of assets and liabilities between the two States
Reorganisation of the State and formation of Telangana
Legal and miscellaneous provisions, including amendments to Articles 168 and 371D
accepted.x: Part I contains the preliminary provisions, including definitions and the population ratio of 58.32:41.68 based on Census 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the subject of the Part to eliminate provisions belonging to neighbouring Parts.
accepted.sec: Act structure - parts, sections, schedules and the subject of each Part  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Parts of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Part III deals with representation in the Legislatures.
2. Part IV deals with the High Court.
3. Part VI deals with apportionment of assets and liabilities.
4. Part VIII deals with provisions as to services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Parts III, IV, VI and VIII cover legislatures, the High Court, assets and liabilities, and services respectively.
accepted.tq: Check each Part-subject pair independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Act structure - parts, sections, schedules and the subject of each Part  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Part)
 a. Part V
 b. Part VII
 c. Part IX
 d. Part X

List-II (Subject)
 i. Infrastructure and Special Economic Measures
 ii. Provisions as to Certain Corporations
 iii. Authorisation of Expenditure and Distribution of Revenues
 iv. Management and Development of Water Resources

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Part V concerns expenditure and revenue distribution; Part VII concerns certain corporations; Part IX concerns water resources; and Part X concerns infrastructure and special economic measures.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Part-subject pair and eliminate codes containing a misplaced subject.
accepted.sec: Act structure - parts, sections, schedules and the subject of each Part  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The provisions relating to amendments of Articles 168 and 371D of the Constitution are contained in:
accepted.x: Part XII contains legal and miscellaneous provisions and amends Articles 168 and 371D.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional amendment with the appropriate concluding Part of the Act.
accepted.sec: Act structure - parts, sections and schedules and the subject of each Part  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the allotment of sitting members of the Rajya Sabha?
accepted.x: The First Schedule provides for allotment of sitting Rajya Sabha members and is linked with Section 13.
accepted.tq: Use the schedule number and its associated legislative subject as a direct recall pair.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Schedule contains amendments to the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 2008?
accepted.x: The Second Schedule contains amendments to the Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 2008, under Section 15.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the first four schedules by linking each to its specific legislative subject.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Seventh Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 contains provisions relating to:
o: Continuance of facilities in State institutions
A list of funds, including provident, pension and insurance funds
accepted.x: The Seventh Schedule provides the list of funds, including provident, pension and insurance funds and other funds.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the adjacent Seventh, Eighth, Ninth and Tenth Schedules by their subjects.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Eleventh Schedule — Coal, oil and gas and power
Eighth Schedule — Government companies and corporations
Ninth Schedule — Apportionment of pension liability
Tenth Schedule — Continuance of facilities in State institutions
accepted.x: The Tenth Schedule concerns continuance of facilities in State institutions, such as APSCHE and Shilparamam. The Eighth concerns pension liability, the Ninth concerns companies and corporations, and the Eleventh concerns river management boards.
accepted.tq: Check the order of closely related schedules and identify the correctly matched pair among deliberate swaps.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ninth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 primarily deals with:
o: Continuance of facilities in State institutions
accepted.x: The Ninth Schedule concerns government companies and corporations, including examples such as APSFC and the Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use representative examples to confirm the subject of the schedule.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: APSHE and Shilparamam are examples associated with which Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
accepted.x: The Tenth Schedule provides for continuance of facilities in State institutions, including APSCHE and Shilparamam.
accepted.tq: Identify the schedule through the institutional examples specifically associated with it.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Schedule lays down the principles for the Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards?
accepted.x: Schedule XI contains the principles for the Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards.
accepted.tq: Link the two named river boards to their common schedule rather than to the water-resources Part alone.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Schedule XI:
1. Irrigation is given precedence over power.
2. Drinking water is given precedence over irrigation.
3. A new project on the Krishna or Godavari may start without Apex Council sanction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A new project on the Krishna or Godavari cannot start without the sanction of the Apex Council, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Spot the negative reversal in the statement concerning mandatory approval.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the ongoing projects identified under Schedule XI?
accepted.x: The identified ongoing projects include Handri Niva, Telugu Ganga, Galeru Nagiri, Veligonda, Kalvakurthi and Nettempadu. Polavaram Left Bank Canal is not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated project list while retaining the similarly named water-resource distractors.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Schedule XII, the equity pattern of Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) is:
accepted.x: Schedule XII provides for SCCL equity of 51 per cent for Telangana and 49 per cent for the Government of India.
accepted.tq: Use the percentage comparison directly and beware of the reversed-share trap.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the power arrangements under Schedule XII is correct?
o: The SLDC was shared for up to six months and APERC for up to two years.
APERC was a joint regulator for up to six months and the SLDC was shared for up to two years.
Central station power was divided equally irrespective of consumption.
Both APERC and the SLDC were shared for up to ten years.
accepted.x: APERC functioned as a joint regulator for up to six months, while the State Load Despatch Centre was shared for up to two years. Central station power was split according to the last five years' consumption.
accepted.tq: Compare the two institutions and their different time limits instead of merging their functions.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A deficit State requiring additional electricity under Schedule XII has:
o: A permanent right to all surplus power of the other State
No preferential right over the other State's surplus power
First right of refusal on the other State's surplus power for ten years
First right of refusal only for two years
accepted.x: A deficit State has the first right of refusal on the surplus power of the other State for a period of ten years.
accepted.tq: Apply the duration and beneficiary conditions to a short power-supply scenario.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following institutions is NOT included among the educational commitments in Schedule XIII?
accepted.x: Schedule XIII includes an IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central, Petroleum and Agricultural Universities, an IIIT, an AIIMS-type hospital, a Tribal University and NIDM. An Indian Institute of Science is not listed.
accepted.tq: Test completeness of a named institutional list by identifying the outside institution.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations is correctly associated with the infrastructure commitments under Schedule XIII?
1. Duggirajupatnam port
2. SAIL steel plant feasibility study in YSR district
3. Vizag-Chennai corridor
4. New railway zone
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four are infrastructure commitments under Schedule XIII. The Schedule also provided for six-month feasibility studies for the steel plant, refinery, Vizag-Chennai corridor and new railway zone.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete list of infrastructure commitments and select the all-inclusive combination.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Vizag-Chennai industrial corridor mentioned in Schedule XIII was modelled on the:
accepted.x: The Vizag-Chennai corridor was modelled on the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor.
accepted.tq: Use the stated model corridor to distinguish the named infrastructure projects.
accepted.sec: Schedules - subject of each (Ninth to Thirteenth in detail)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was to function as the common capital for a period of:
accepted.x: Section 5 provided for Hyderabad to serve as the common capital for up to ten years, after which it would be the capital of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh would have a new capital.
accepted.tq: Test the statutory time limit and distinguish a transitional arrangement from a permanent one.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which provision directed the Centre to constitute an expert committee on the capital of Andhra Pradesh within six months?
accepted.x: Section 6 required the Centre to set up an expert committee on the capital of Andhra Pradesh within six months.
accepted.tq: Distinguish consecutive sections by matching the specific institutional action to its section number.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the provisions of Sections 7 and 8?
o: They provide for the national project status of Polavaram.
They provide for the Apex Council and the two river management boards.
They provide for a common Governor and the Governor's special responsibility in the common capital.
They provide for tax incentives and capital infrastructure support.
accepted.x: Sections 7 and 8 deal with the common Governor and the Governor's special responsibility in the common capital.
accepted.tq: Identify the pair of related provisions and avoid confusing them with water or financial provisions.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 10 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 amended the First Schedule of the Constitution to provide for Telangana as the:
accepted.x: Section 10 amended the First Schedule of the Constitution and recognised Telangana as the 29th State of India.
accepted.tq: Connect the section with the constitutional schedule and the resulting ordinal number.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 46 provided for the distribution of the Thirteenth Finance Commission award on the basis of:
o: Equal division between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana only
Population ratio and other relevant parameters
accepted.x: Section 46 provided for splitting the Thirteenth Finance Commission award using the population ratio and other parameters. It also provided grants and a special development package for backward areas, especially Rayalaseema and North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Prefer the precise multi-factor statement over an extreme single-factor allocation claim.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Apex Council constituted under Section 84 consists of:
o: The Prime Minister as Chairperson and the Governors of both States, with four members
The Union Water Resources Minister as Chairperson and the Chief Ministers of both States, with three members
The Chief Ministers of both States as joint Chairpersons, with six members
The Union Finance Minister as Chairperson and both Chief Secretaries, with two members
accepted.x: Section 84 provides for an Apex Council chaired by the Union Water Resources Minister, with the Chief Ministers of both States and three members.
accepted.tq: Check the composition and chairperson separately to catch wrong-authority substitutions.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Sections 85 and 89:
1. The Godavari River Management Board has its headquarters in Telangana.
2. The Krishna River Management Board has its headquarters in Andhra Pradesh.
3. The term of the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal was extended for project-wise allocation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Section 85 provides for the GRMB at Telangana and KRMB at Andhra Pradesh, while Section 89 extends the KWDT term for project-wise allocation.
accepted.tq: Combine related provisions while preserving the distinction between river boards and the tribunal.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which authority was assigned responsibility for security of the Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards?
accepted.x: Section 85 provided for security of the river management boards by the Central Industrial Security Force.
accepted.tq: Use the responsible security organisation as the decisive institutional clue.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 91 dealt with arrangements concerning the:
o: Tungabhadra Board, including HLC, LLC and Rajolibanda
Godavari and Krishna River Management Boards
accepted.x: Section 91 concerns Tungabhadra Board arrangements relating to the HLC, LLC and Rajolibanda systems.
accepted.tq: Match the section with its specific project arrangement rather than with the broader river-board framework.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94) [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 93, the Centre was required to take the measures specified in the Thirteenth Schedule within:
accepted.x: Section 93 required the Centre to take the measures specified in the Thirteenth Schedule within ten years.
accepted.tq: Test the implementation period separately from the ten-year common-capital period.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the forms of support contemplated under Section 94?
o: Permanent exemption of all State taxes
Special financial support for capital infrastructure
accepted.x: Section 94 provided for tax incentives, backward-area programmes, special financial support for capital infrastructure, and denotification of degraded forest land for the capital. It did not provide a permanent exemption from all State taxes.
accepted.tq: Identify the overbroad fiscal claim that goes beyond the listed statutory measures.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Special financial support under Section 94 for the capital of Andhra Pradesh included provision for which group of institutions?
o: IIT, IIM, NIT and AIIMS only
Municipal corporations, district courts and panchayat offices only
Raj Bhavan, High Court, Secretariat, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
Parliament, Supreme Court, Election Commission and UPSC
accepted.x: Section 94 contemplated special financial support for capital infrastructure, including Raj Bhavan, the High Court, Secretariat, Assembly and Council.
accepted.tq: Use the complete institutional cluster to distinguish capital infrastructure from educational commitments.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Section 94 also permitted the denotification of which land for the capital?
o: Agricultural land under permanent forest status
accepted.x: Section 94 provided for denotification of degraded forest land for the capital.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact legal description of land instead of substituting a broader land category.
accepted.sec: Key sections - provisions (5, 8, 46, 84-91, 93, 94)  [APPSC]
